{
  "response": "## Adapter-key ordering assertions

In `tests/test_requests.py`, within `test_transport_adapter_ordering`, the initial assertion requires a new session's adapter keys to be ordered as `["https://", "http://"]`:

```python
order = ["https://", "http://"]
assert order == list(s.adapters)
```

After mounting `http://git`, `http://github`, `http://github.com`, and `http://github.com/about/`, the test asserts longest/more-specific prefixes first, followed by the default HTTPS and HTTP keys:

```python
assert order == list(s.adapters)
```

with the expected order being `http://github.com/about/`, `http://github.com`, `http://github`, `http://git`, `https://`, and `http://`. It then mounts the `gittip` variants and makes another `assert order == list(s.adapters)`, expecting each group to remain ordered from the most specific key to the least specific key, followed by `https://` and `http://`. [Data: Sources (91); Entities (1261)]

The test also checks that replacing `s2.adapters` with an HTTP mapping and then mounting HTTPS retains both `"http://"` and `"https://"`, but those are membership assertions rather than adapter-key ordering assertions. [Data: Sources (91)]

The supplied snapshot identifies the test and its source block but does not provide more precise line numbers for each individual assertion within `test_requests.py:L1488-L1634`.",
  "score": 96,
  "follow_up_queries": [
    "Which session adapter selection loop implements the ordering asserted by test_transport_adapter_ordering?",
    "Which tests assert longest-prefix matching and case-insensitive adapter-prefix matching?"
  ]
}
